items.name: Certificate of formation
items.agency: NJ Division of Revenue and Enterprise Services
items.quote: First, file a Certificate of formation/authorization.

items.name: Employer Identification Number (EIN)
items.quote: You never have to pay a fee for an EIN.
items.feeQuote: You never have to pay a fee for an EIN.

items.name: Tax and employer registration (NJ-REG)
items.agency: NJ Division of Revenue and Enterprise Services
items.quote: Second, after filing the certificate of formation/authorization, file the tax/employer registration form (Form NJ-REG).

items.name: Food establishment plan review
items.quote: A permit applicant or operator shall submit to the health authority properly prepared plans and specifications for review and approval before:

items.name: Jersey City Certificate of Occupancy
items.quote: Per City Code, a Certificate of Occupancy is required for new construction, major renovations or changes in building use.

items.name: Construction permit for the build-out
items.quote: you will need to apply for the appropriate construction applications and pass inspections before applying for a Certificate of Occupancy.

items.name: Retail food establishment license
items.agency: Jersey City Department of Health and Human Services
items.quote: Find HHS licensing applications for beauty salons, barbershops, body art, kennels, pet shops, shelters and retail food establishments.

items.name: Workers' compensation insurance
items.agency: New Jersey Department of Labor, Division of Workers' Compensation
items.note: Added in the coverage audit of 2026-10-22: bought from an insurer once there is staff.
items.quote: All corporations operating in New Jersey must maintain Workers' Compensation insurance or be approved for self-insurance
